title: Not All Mislabels Are Equal: Efficient Task-Aware Auditing with Confidence Sequences
abstract: arXiv:2610.33262v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study efficient, adaptive auditing of categorical labels in a fixed dataset, motivated by biodiversity-credit programs in which expert verification of species records is costly and downstream scores (e.g., payment) are more sensitive to errors on certain labels than on others. Our proposed ATLAS framework couples anytime-valid inference with a task-aware adaptive auditing policy. Representing label corrections through a confusion matrix, we prioritize which data points to inspect next based on both label uncertainty and the influence of potential label corrections on the downstream score function. For linear scores such as the mislabel rate, our priority-aware approach certifies the overall label error rate to $\pm 2$ percentage points with 24% and 11% fewer audits than random sampling on biodiversity data from Kenya and a widely used CIFAR-10N benchmark, respectively. translated_title: 并非所有错误标签都同等重要：基于置信序列的高效任务感知审计
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.33262v1 公告类型：交叉。摘要：我们研究在固定数据集中对类别标签进行高效、自适应的审计，其动机来自生物多样性信用项目：在这类项目中，专家验证物种记录的成本高昂，且下游评分（如付款金额）对某些标签上错误的敏感度高于其他标签。我们提出的ATLAS框架将任意时刻有效推断与任务感知的自适应审计策略相结合。通过混淆矩阵来表示标签修正，我们根据标签不确定性以及潜在标签修正对下游评分函数的影响，来决定接下来优先检查哪些数据点。对于误标率等线性评分，我们的优先级感知方法在肯尼亚生物多样性数据和广泛使用的CIFAR-10N基准数据集上，分别以比随机抽样少24%和11%的审计量，将整体标签错误率认证到±2个百分点的精度。对于希尔-香农多样性等非线性评分，我们探讨了（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文提出ATLAS框架，将任意时刻有效的置信序列推断与任务感知的自适应审计策略结合，根据标签不确定性及其对下游评分的影响优先审计数据点，从而以比随机抽样少11%-24%的审计量将标签错误率认证到±2个百分点的精度。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes ATLAS, a framework that couples anytime-valid confidence sequences with a task-aware adaptive auditing policy that prioritizes data points by label uncertainty and their impact on downstream scores, certifying label error rates to ±2 percentage points with 11-24% fewer audits than random sampling.
